newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican teachers call off strike, head back home.
newsitem.headline: Mexican teachers call off strike, head back home.

text.p: Thousands of teachers from across Mexico returned to their homes from Mexico City on Saturday after calling off a month of protest marches and strikes that caused traffic havoc in the huge capital.

The public schoolteachers, part of the dissident National Coordinating Council of Education Workers (CNTE), called off the strike late on Friday after making some progress with authorities in their demands for a wage hike.
The teachers said they would continue talks with local officials in their states, but warned they would return to the capital again if their demands were not fully met.

In early May, the government announced a salary rise of six percent for teachers plus an extra 10 percent in bonuses. The teachers called that ridiculous, saying their real salaries were dropping because of high inflation.
Teachers said their salaries ranged from about 600 pesos ($75) to 1,400 pesos ($177) every two weeks.
